score.note: Improved from a prior draft (400/207/140) by three idiom-matched respellings, each verified against the reference disassembly before adoption: (1) writing scale_y before scale_x in both spawn sites, matching the reference's str-offset-28-then-24 order exactly at both sites; (2) spelling the repeat-loop's `(index & 3) ? 9 : 10` call argument as an explicit if/else with the Func_08009240 call duplicated in each branch (matching the reference's two separate bl sites and .L4/.L5 labels) rather than as a single branchless ternary, which the compiler had compiled into a NEG/ORR/LSR boolean-normalize sequence not present in the reference; (3) introducing a second local (`particle`) aliased from the second spawned object's pointer, used specifically for the repeat-loop calls, the post-loop unconditional call, and the long_delay null check, while `object` continues to cover the field-write blocks and the remaining null checks -- this reduced wrong_instructions from 132 to 123 despite not fully reproducing the reference's register split (below). The remaining 207-halfword residual is concentrated in one region: the reference promotes three cross-call scalars into high registers (sl=state, r8/r9 shared across the link accumulator/link_marker/loop-invariant AND-mask) and keeps two live registers (r5 and r6) simultaneously bound to the identical second-spawned-object pointer at different call/check sites, while this compiler's value-numbering coalesces any two locals proven equal (confirmed: the `particle = object` copy itself is eliminated, and swapping which named local is read at which site produces byte-identical output), so it always keeps that pointer in a single register (r5) and only ever needs two high registers (r8, sl) rather than three. This is a genuine register-allocator sensitivity, not a semantic gap -- the field/call/branch structure, offsets, constants, and control flow all match the reference exactly wherever the diff aligns; every remaining `!` line is a register-name or literal-pool-offset consequence of this one allocation difference.

rejected_experiments: Swapping index++/Func_080030f8(1) statement order in the first loop (call before increment instead of after): regressed 207->209 differing_halfwords; reverted.

Swapping which of object/particle is assigned first from the spawn call (object=call();particle=object; vs particle=call();object=particle;) with usage sites held fixed: byte-identical output in both directions, confirming the compiler coalesces by proven value equality, not by source-level variable identity.

Collapsing back to a single `object` local for the whole function (dropping the particle alias) after the if/else ternary fix: regressed wrong_instructions 123->131; the two-local split is a net win even though it does not reproduce the reference's r5/r6 register split.
